name: N'Ko Script
notes: Created by Solomana Kanté (Souleymane Kanté) in Guinea/Côte d'Ivoire, completed 1949, after experimenting with and rejecting adaptations of Arabic and Latin script for Maninka's tone/vowel system. Visually resembles Arabic script (cursive, right-to-left) but is structurally a genuine alphabet with obligatory tone marking, built from scratch rather than adapted sign-by-sign from Arabic. The oft-repeated motivating anecdote (a Lebanese journalist claiming African languages were "unwritable") is well-attested as N'Ko community history but not independently confirmed outside that tradition — flagged accordingly. Still in active use — `latest: null`.
